license.payload: Per item, recorded in origin.items. Every paper was first published 1925–1928 and is in the public domain in the United States (published before 1931, the term of 95 years run). The terms of life plus seventy years still run in the European Union and the United Kingdom: Pauli (d. 1958) to 2028, so free from 2029-01-01; Schrödinger (d. 1961) from 2032-01-01; Bohr (d. 1962) from 2033-01-01; Born (d. 1970) from 2041-01-01; Heisenberg (d. 1976) from 2047-01-01; Jordan (d. 1980) from 2051-01-01, which governs the two papers written with Born and with Born and Heisenberg; Dirac (d. 1984) from 2055-01-01. The seat holds the texts under United States public domain, the archive's jurisdiction. The Zeitschrift für Physik volumes are Internet Archive scans in the collection of the University of Illinois Chicago (uic); the Annalen and Naturwissenschaften issues are the Archive's microfilm series (sim_microfilm); the Proceedings volume is a Digital Library of India scan (dc.rights: Not Available). None of these items carries a rights or licence field.

normalization: Originals as fetched under original/: the Internet Archive's OCR layers (_djvu.txt), each md5 matching the one the Archive publishes. text/<slug>.ocr.txt is that layer with line endings normalized. All scans are held by reference (identifier, file, size and md5): each is a whole volume or issue carrying many papers. The OCR of the Zeitschrift für Physik volumes often reads ü as ii and ß as B; the loci avoid such words where they can and say so where they cannot. No text was corrected by hand.
scope: Held: every paper the ruling names, each in the volume or issue that first printed it: Pauli's exclusion principle (Z. Physik 31), Heisenberg's Umdeutung (Z. Physik 33), Born and Jordan (Z. Physik 34), Born, Heisenberg and Jordan (Z. Physik 35), Schrödinger's four communications (Annalen 79, 80, 81), Dirac's electron (Proc. R. Soc. A 117), and Bohr's Como lecture in its German printing (Naturwissenschaften 16). The Zeitschrift volumes are seated whole, so the same witnesses also carry the other papers of 1925–26 printed beside these. Not held: Dirac's second part, “The Quantum Theory of the Electron. Part II” (Proc. R. Soc. A 118, 1928, 351–361), not sought this session; the English printing of the Como lecture (Nature 121, 1928, supplement, 580–590), not sought; Heisenberg's uncertainty paper (Z. Physik 43, 1927, 172–198), outside the ruling's list, on the Archive under the item zeitschrift-fur-physik-vol-43 (not opened this session) and left for a later seating.

why_seated: Between January 1925 and January 1928 a handful of papers rebuilt the description of the atom twice, once as matrices and once as waves, and then joined both to relativity. The seat holds each in the pages where it first appeared, so that the claims later made for them can be checked against the words that made them. The European terms still run for all of them; in the United States they are already open.
